title: Slow-path admission and response fidelity transforms for tiered load shedding
creator: Maya Chen
description: Implement a slow-path admission and response-fidelity transformation system that provides an intermediate degradation tier between full-quality responses and hard rejection. The goal is to preserve availability and SLO compliance during multi-region capacity pressure by: 1) admitting lower-priority requests into a slow-path worker pool instead of outright shedding them, and 2) applying deterministic, auditable fidelity transforms to responses (context trimming, early-summary, compressed token formats, and structured stubs). This ticket covers design, runtime admission hooks, transform library, telemetry, and rollout plan.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Slow-path admission algorithm implemented and gated by feature flag; can be toggled per-region and per-tenant.
A2: Three fidelity transforms implemented: CONTEXT_TRIM, SUMMARY_STUB, and EMBEDDING_APPROX. Each transform exposes deterministic, testable contracts and metrics for quality regression checks.

A3: End-to-end latency SLOs preserved for P1/P0 tenants (99th percentile within configured tier); lower-priority tenants routed to slow-path with measurable added latency but maintained success rate >95% under target load.
A4: Grafana dashboards show slow-path admission rate, transform rates, per-tenant quality deltas, and token-cost savings; alerts for transform-induced QA regressions are wired into PagerDuty.
A5: Canary rollout in eu-central-1 with 5% traffic for one week, with automatic rollback if quality regression >5% on baseline eval prompts.
A6: Documentation (Confluence) and runbook updated describing operator controls, safe rollback, and post-incident analysis steps.
implementation_notes: Design an admission score: score = alpha * tenant_priority + beta * recent_error_rate + gamma * remaining_token_budget. Score thresholds decide fast-path, slow-path, or shed.
Expose admission decisions in request tracing headers for debugging (X-RW-Admission: fast|slow|shed) and record reason codes (capacity, region-overload, tenant-credit).
Implement transform library in runtime service as pure functions with deterministic checksum to allow later replay/validation.
Slow-path workers run on a lower-priority GPU pool with larger batching windows and optional model-quantized variants; responses go through transform pipeline before returning.
Provide a graceful rehydration API: clients can request a 'full' re-eval later (background patching) if slow-path returned a stub and tenant has credits.
Integrate with Console: per-route toggle for enabling slow-path, per-tenant override, and visibility into historical transform usage and cost savings.
Telemetry: emit metrics tokens_saved_by_transform, quality_delta_{metric}, slow_path_admit_rate, slow_path_p95_latency, and transform_error_rate.
Testing: unit tests for each transform, integration tests simulating overload using synthetic traffic in staging, and automated quality checks using stored prompt-eval sets.
